clue.text: In English city a bear causes pandemonium

parts.note: Hull is a city in Yorkshire, England
Baloo is the bear in Kipling's The Jungle Book

explanation.surface: A bear loose in an English city sets off chaos in the streets.
explanation.walkthrough: BALOO is the bear in Kipling's The Jungle Book, so 'bear' points to a name here, not to an ordinary word for the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a noisy uproar, a scene of wild confusion.

clue.text: Junior on work experience

to go is to function or work, as a machine does

explanation.surface: A junior employee on a work-experience placement.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places UNDER above GO.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something is to experience or go through it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Fastening some in chapel at Christmas

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Decorations being fixed up in a chapel at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: A latch is a simple bar or catch that keeps a door or gate closed, a kind of fastening.

clue.text: A barn owl agitated former PM

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up or disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A barn owl frightened a former prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew Bonar Law was the British Prime Minister in 1922-23.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonar Law led a Conservative government in the early 1920s, so he is a past premier.

clue.text: Behave uninhibitedly? Soon draw the line at work

clue.text: Apartment taken in outskirts of Oundle, recently

explanation.walkthrough: Oundle is a small market town in Northamptonshire, England; only its outer letters matter here.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an adverb meaning lately, in the recent past.

clue.text: Film icon getting rid of old clothes

clue.text: American soldier restraining a coarse Italian patriot

parts.note: GI is the standard term for a US soldier

clue.text: Almost chance one and only fried meatball

clue.text: Part of packed itinerary ready for publication

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.definitionFit: To prepare text for publication by correcting and revising it is to give it an editorial pass, a verb sense.

clue.text: Skin condition affected her talents

clue.text: Arrives to entertain revolutionary bowman

clue.text: College backing up reserve computer

explanation.walkthrough: The IT sense of 'backing up' fits the computer surface, disguising the turnaround signal.

clue.text: Better money for army chiefs, maybe

explanation.walkthrough: BRASS is northern British slang for money.

explanation.definitionFit: Bombay mix is a crunchy savoury mixture of fried lentils, nuts and noodles, served as a spicy nibble.

clue.text: German song told a story

clue.text: Couple in conversation decline sweet

explanation.surface: Two people talking about a fall in sweetness.
explanation.walkthrough: A pear drop is a British boiled sweet flavoured like pears.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear drop is a hard boiled candy, so a sweet in the British sense.

clue.text: Circulated plans for junk mail

parts.note: maps are plans of an area or building

explanation.surface: Distributed plans that end up as unwanted post.

clue.text: Squad also included in scheme

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
too means also

clue.text: Rum at pier provided, as a drink to whet one's appetite

clue.text: I do it wrongly, in charge — that's very stupid

clue.text: Charlie knocked over tin — go for a brandy

clue.text: Short lament by soldier's lover

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper; the 's is read as 'is', linking to the definition

parts.note: to mourn is to lament

explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' gives MOUR; the 's on 'soldier's' stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.

clue.text: Talk inconsequentially with religious leader close to minaret

clue.text: Hat left out in arbour
